headlines.title: Community rallies after East Bay coffee trailer burglarized hours after owners welcome premature baby
headlines.description: An East Bay couple experienced a rollercoaster of emotions after welcoming a premature baby, only to have their small business burglarized less than 24 hours later. Christian Thorn shared the news on social media after thieves targeted the couple’s mobile coffee trailer, the Quenched Trailer, early Friday morning. “Instead of being with my wife and child I am dealing with a generator that is stolen,” Thorn said in an Instagram video. “Somebody came and drilled the generator out and stole it at 5 in the morning.” Thorn and his wife, Cam, operate the mobile business in a Concord parking lot. “We are a legit small business, that’s our livelihood,” Thorn said. “We need the generator to keep the trailer running to pay the bills.” While Cam and their newborn daughter, Charlotte, recovered in the hospital, the local community rallied behind the family. A GoFundMe campaign generated financial support, allowing Thorn to purchase a replacement generator and get the Quenched Trailer brewing coffee once again. “It’s terrible. I really feel bad for them. It’s good that they’re here and we’re here to support them,” said customer Ibrahim Elradi. Barista Lake Juranek noted that the trailer was her boss Cam’s pride and joy. “Her heart and soul has been poured into this place, so it’s really crazy,” Juranek said, adding, “It was her baby until we actually had a baby.” Despite a tough week, Thorn said baby Charlotte is slowly getting stronger while remaining on a feeding tube and oxygen. The family remains overwhelmed by the outpouring of love for both their new baby and their business. “That was just an overwhelming support,” Thorn said. “We are just amazed how many people we’ve touched and they’ve helped us.” The couple hopes to raise enough money to install a security system and eventually expand to an indoor location inside the Sloat Garden Center.
